# Writing encounters

> **The easy way: the creator dashboard.** Run `npm run creator` and open
> <http://localhost:4321>. It lists every kind of content (encounters, tiles and locations,
> adventures, Fate cards, items, hero classes, riddles and table rules) with forms that show
> what's required and every option there is, including pickers for runes, tiles, locations, items
> and icons, and has a board editor for painting places onto the board's squares. Saving checks the change against the same schemas as the tests and writes straight
> to these files, in this repo's formatting; "Run content checks" runs the content tests. New hero
> classes and adventures are listed in the app's manifests for you. Your own SVG or PNG art can
> be added in the icon picker: it's saved in `content/art/`, listed for the app in
> `src/content/art.ts`, and named in icons as `art:<name>`. It's developer-only: it runs on your
> computer and never ships in the app. The rest of this page is the reference behind it.

Each board tile has one JSON file in [`tiles/`](tiles/) (`civilization.json`, `dungeon.json`, ...).
The format is defined in [`schema.json`](schema.json). Editors like VS Code read the
`"$schema"` line at the top of each file and will autocomplete fields and underline mistakes as you type.

Check your changes before committing:

```
npm test
```

This also runs in CI on every push and pull request to `develop` and `main`.
If you change the format itself, also update the matching types in `src/content/types.ts`.

## Structure

```
tile                      e.g. Civilization
└── locations[]           the board's symbols, e.g. City, Sewer, Cemetery, Mini Boss, Boss
    └── encounters[]      one is drawn at random when a hero lands on that location
        └── actions[]     what the player can do: roll, choice or shop
```

## The board

[`board.json`](board.json) lays the tiles out as the digital board:

- `size`: how many squares across (and down) each tile is.
- `tiles[]`: each tile's `origin` (its top-left square on the whole board, `[x, y]`) and its `squares`, row by row from the top, each a location id from that tile.
- `journey`: the tiles in the order heroes travel them (clockwise: Civilization, Wilderness, Dungeon, Chaos). A hero crosses between two tiles only if they're next to each other on the journey, through the edge they share, either way. Tiles that aren't neighbours on the journey never connect, even side by side.
- `start`: the squares heroes start on, in turn order, `[x, y]`. There's one for every player who can join.

The layout is a draft for now; the content tests check every square names a real location, the tiles don't overlap, and each pair on the journey shares an edge.

## Encounters

| Field         | Required   | Notes                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | yes        | `<tile>.<location>.<name>`, e.g. `civilization.cities.greedy-guards`. Must be unique. |
| `status`      | yes        | `draft` while you're writing it, `ready` when it's complete.                          |
| `title`       | when ready |                                                                                       |
| `description` | yes        | The situation, shown to the player.                                                   |
| `tags`        | when ready | What it's about, from the list below. Never changes how it plays.                     |
| `actions`     | yes        | At least one. Mix types freely, e.g. a shop plus a Charisma roll to haggle.           |
| `turnedAway`  | no         | Turns away heroes with poor renown. See [Renown](#renown).                            |
| `boss`        | no         | `mini` or `boss`. Shown as one; its fight's victory must award a `fate` draw.         |
| `notes`       | no         | For authors only; never shown in the app.                                             |

**Drafts vs ready.** Drafts appear in the app marked **DRAFT** so they can be playtested.
Each action type's _structure_ is checked even in drafts (a shop must have items, a roll must have a stat),
so you can't create something broken by accident. _Polish_ is only required once `ready`: titles, tags,
difficulties, prices, and every outcome's `result` (story `text` is optional).

**Tags:** `social`, `financial`, `combat`, `exploration`, `magic`, `stealth`, `shop`, `item-shop`, `tavern`, `trap`.
New tags are added to the `tag` list in `schema.json` (and the `Tag` type in `src/content/types.ts`).

## Actions

The `type` decides which screen appears, what data is required and what can happen.

### `roll`: dice against a stat, or a coin flip

```json
{
  "type": "roll",
  "stat": "STR",
  "difficulty": 16,
  "description": "Grasp the pole and heave the manhole open.",
  "pass": { ... },
  "fail": { ... }
}
```

- `stat` is one of the six stats, `STR` (Strength), `DEX` (Dexterity), `STL` (Stealth), `SUR`
  (Survival), `ATK` (Attack) or `DEF` (Defense), or `coin` to call and flip a coin. The button shows
  its name unless you set `label`.
- For a stat, the hero rolls one d6 per point and must reach `difficulty` ("Roll your Strength VS 16").
  A coin flip has no difficulty.
- **Luck checks** (`"stat": "coin"`): the encounter must be tagged `luck` (the content tests check
  both ways). With **Digital coin tosses** on in Settings, the player tosses a coin on screen
  instead: crown passes, skull fails. Only coin checks ever get the coin.
- The players roll real dice (or flip a real coin) at the table and tap **Pass** or **Fail**. Rename
  those buttons with `passLabel` / `failLabel`.
- Results use each theme's dice wording ("Triumph!" / "Doom!").
- `cost` makes it a **class option**, paid from a class resource:
  `"cost": { "resource": "magic", "amount": 5 }`. Only heroes of that class see it, they need that
  much to try, and it's spent whether they pass or fail. For "−5 more" on a failure, add a
  `resource` effect to `fail`.

| Class   | Resource      |
| ------- | ------------- |
| Warrior | `rage`        |
| Mage    | `magic`       |
| Devout  | `faith`       |
| Druid   | `primal`      |
| Ranger  | `reflex`      |
| Thief   | `skulduggery` |

Every encounter must keep at least one action that any hero can take.

### `choice`: pick one of 1–4 options, no dice

```json
{
  "type": "choice",
  "label": "Pay the toll",
  "description": "Give the guard payment.",
  "requirement": "You can only pay if you have at least 1 gold.",
  "options": [
    { "id": "pay", "label": "Pay 1 gold", "tone": "neutral", "outcome": { ... } },
    { "id": "refuse", "label": "Can't/Don't Pay", "tone": "neutral", "outcome": { ... } }
  ]
}
```

- `requirement` (optional) is shown above the buttons.
- Each option has its own `outcome`, and a **tone** that says what kind of option it is:

| Tone       | Use it for                                    | Looks like (in most themes)                   |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `positive` | clearly good for the hero                     | the theme's "good" colour, triumphant wording |
| `neutral`  | neither good nor bad, e.g. paying or refusing | an outline, calm wording ("So It Goes")       |
| `negative` | clearly bad                                   | the theme's "bad" colour, doom-laden wording  |
| `special`  | strange, magical or surprising                | the theme's accent colour, mysterious wording |

- An option can set its own result `title`; otherwise the theme's wording for its tone is used.
- Option `id`s must be unique within the action.

### `shop`: buy something or walk away, no dice

```json
{
  "type": "shop",
  "id": "wares",
  "label": "Browse the wares",
  "description": "Peruse their wares.",
  "items": [
    { "id": "silver-sword", "name": "Silver Sword", "price": 10, "bonus": "+1 STR", "stock": 1 }
  ],
  "restock": { "rule": "everyNRounds", "every": 3 },
  "leave": {
    "text": "The merchant grumbles and wanders away.",
    "result": "Move as normal next turn."
  }
}
```

- `id` identifies the shop's stock during a game; unique within the encounter. Item `id`s are unique within the shop.
- Buying automatically takes the `price` in gold and adds the item. Add extra `effects` to an item if buying it does more.
- `stock` is how many the shop has; leave it out for unlimited. Stock is shared by all players in a game.
- `restock` decides when sold-out stock comes back: `never`, `everyRound`, `everyNRounds` (with `every`),
  or `shuffle` (with `display`: offer that many items at random from the list, re-drawn each round).
- `leave` is what happens when the player walks away.

### `fight`: battle a foe over several exchanges

```json
{
  "type": "fight",
  "label": "Fight the Warden",
  "description": "Stand your ground against the Warden and his chains.",
  "foe": { "name": "The Warden of Chains", "wounds": 3, "strike": 2 },
  "moves": [
    { "label": "Batter through his guard", "stat": "STR", "difficulty": 16 },
    { "label": "Unbind the chains", "stat": "ATK", "difficulty": 20 }
  ],
  "victory": { ... },
  "defeat": { ... },
  "flee": { ... }
}
```

- Each exchange, the hero picks one of the 1–4 `moves` and rolls at the table. **Pass** and the foe
  takes a wound; **fail** and the foe strikes back for `strike` health.
- The foe falls after `wounds` passes (`victory`). If the strikes take the hero's last health, it's
  `defeat`. With a `flee` outcome, the hero can run between exchanges.
- The health lost to strikes is applied automatically and shown on the result, so don't repeat it in
  the outcomes.
- Once the first blow lands there's no backing out: the fight is seen through.
- **Bosses:** give the encounter `"boss": "mini"` or `"boss": "boss"`, and put it in its tile's
  `mini-boss` or `boss` location. Every tile has both, as every tile on the board does. A boss's
  fight must award a draw from the Chest of Fate on victory (`{ "type": "fate" }`); the content
  tests check all this.
- **Coming soon:** a location with no encounters yet is on the board, so it's listed, but dimmed
  as "Coming soon" and can't be picked. Write an encounter for it and it opens.

### `puzzle`: answer a riddle

A puzzle asks its own riddle, or one from the shared pool in [`riddles.json`](riddles.json):

```json
{
  "type": "puzzle",
  "label": "Answer the inscription",
  "intro": "The inscription reads",
  "description": "Words are carved above the sealed door.",
  "fromPool": true,
  "success": { ... },
  "failure": { ... }
}
```

- **Its own riddle:** put the riddle in `description`, list 2–4 `answers` (`id` and `label`), and set
  `correct` to the right answer's `id`.
- **From the pool:** set `"fromPool": true` and leave out `answers` and `correct`. `description` is then
  the scene on the puzzle's button. Write `success` and `failure` so they fit any riddle. In a game, the
  pool is shuffled once and dealt one riddle per turn, so riddles don't repeat until every one has been
  asked. Backing out and coming back shows the same riddle.
- `guesses` (default 1) is how many answers the hero may try; a wrong one is struck out. It must be
  fewer than the answers, and pool riddles always have 4.
- **Adding a riddle to the pool:** add it to `riddles.json` with a unique `id`, the `question`, exactly
  4 `answers`, and the `correct` one. Make sure only one answer really fits.

## The Chest of Fate

The only physical cards are the **Chest of Fate**: Fate cards with a leather pouch on the back and
four runes on the face. They're for extraordinary deeds: give an outcome a `fate` effect, e.g. for
defeating a boss or a mini-boss, and the result screen opens the chest before the turn can end. The
player draws a card and taps its runes; if they match, its reward is revealed and applied.

The cards are in [`fate.json`](fate.json) (schema: [`fate.schema.json`](fate.schema.json)):

```json
{
  "id": "emberheart-amulet",
  "runes": ["sun", "star", "skull", "diamond"],
  "name": "Emberheart Amulet",
  "rarity": "legendary",
  "text": "Warm as a hearth in the coldest crypt.",
  "effects": [{ "type": "item", "name": "Emberheart Amulet" }]
}
```

- `runes`: four of the twelve (`sun`, `moon`, `star`, `flame`, `water`, `leaf`, `skull`, `eye`, `diamond`,
  `crown`, `key`, `feather`), left to right. **Any two cards must differ in at least two runes**, so one
  wrong tap never opens someone else's card. The content tests check this.
- `effects` are applied automatically. An item must be in `items.json` with a `slot`; it goes straight
  on if its place is free, otherwise into the pack.
- Each card's reward can be claimed **once per game**; the deck goes back in the chest for the next.
- **Testing:** four skulls open a debug card, _The Debug Stone_, as often as you like. It's defined in
  `src/content/debug.ts`; **remove it before launch** (every place it's hooked in says so).
- **Printing:** `node tools/fate-cards.mjs fate-cards.html`, then print it double-sided (flip on the
  long edge) at 100%. Faces and backs line up, nine poker-size cards to a page.

## Renown

A hero's renown is how well known their deeds are, for good or ill, and it can go below 0. It's also
their experience: every 50 renown earns a level. Encounters can react to it in two ways.

- **`standing` on any action** locks it for heroes below `atLeast`. The button still shows, with what it
  needs, but can't be picked. For example, guards who might recognise a hero with 15 or more renown:
  `"standing": { "atLeast": 15 }`. At least one action in each encounter must stay open.
- **`turnedAway` on an encounter** stops a hero whose renown is `atMost` or lower before they can do
  anything. They get its `outcome` instead (with an optional result `title`), and that's their turn:

```json
"turnedAway": {
  "atMost": -3,
  "title": "Run Out of Town",
  "outcome": {
    "text": "The guards know your face...",
    "result": "Move your hero to the nearest Sewers.",
    "effects": [{ "type": "moveTo", "location": "civilization.sewers" }]
  }
}
```

Levels: −3 Hated, −2 Distrusted, −1 Disliked, 0 Unknown, +1 Welcome, +2 Trusted, +3 Honored.

## Outcomes

```json
{
  "text": "You toss a coin to the guard and go along your merry way.",
  "result": "Lose 1 gold.",
  "effects": [{ "type": "gold", "amount": -1 }]
}
```

- `text`: the story, shown to the player.
- `result`: the game instruction players apply, in plain words.
- `effects`: optional. The same instruction in a form the app can act on: during a game, the
  character tracker applies them to the current hero's sheet. If a result can't be fully expressed as effects (for example a choice, or
  something conditional), leave `effects` out rather than writing only part of it, and explain why in `notes`.
- `table`: with `effects`, the rest of the result that players do at the table and the app doesn't
  track, such as board movement, Gear cards or a lost turn: `"table": "+1 Gear. Free Movement."`
- `leadsTo`: carries on to another action in the same encounter, by its index (0 is the first). For
  example, a failed escape that says "Go to the Fight option" has `"leadsTo": 1` if Fight is the
  second action. The turn doesn't end until that action is played out.
- A `roll` with `"stat": "combat"` is a fight played out at the table with Andrew's combat rules;
  list who the hero fights in `enemies` (name, `count`, and `stats` in the book's order). The
  buttons read Victory and Defeat. A roll can also be opposed: instead of a `difficulty`, set
  `versus`, e.g. `"versus": "the guards' Dexterity (3d6)"`.
- The `slain` effect kills the hero outright: their health drops to 0 and they have fallen.

| Effect         | Fields                                                   | Example                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gold`         | `amount`                                                 | `{ "type": "gold", "amount": -5 }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `renown`       | `amount`                                                 | `{ "type": "renown", "amount": 1 }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `item`         | `name`, optional `amount`                                | `{ "type": "item", "name": "Glowing Marble" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `card`         | `name`                                                   | `{ "type": "card", "name": "Into the Deep" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `moveTo`       | `location` as `<tile>.<location>`                        | `{ "type": "moveTo", "location": "civilization.graveyards" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `stay`         |                                                          | `{ "type": "stay" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `health`       | `amount`                                                 | `{ "type": "health", "amount": -2 }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `resource`     | `amount`                                                 | `{ "type": "resource", "amount": -5 }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `fate`         |                                                          | `{ "type": "fate" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `move`         | `direction` (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW), `squares`      | `{ "type": "move", "direction": "S", "squares": 1 }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `freeMovement` | optional `extra`, optional `orTo` (a place on this tile) | `{ "type": "freeMovement", "extra": 1 }`, `{ "type": "freeMovement", "orTo": "coin" }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `halveHealth`  |                                                          | `{ "type": "halveHealth" }`: lose half your health, rounded in your favour, never below 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `loseTurn`     | optional `turns` (default 1)                             | `{ "type": "loseTurn" }`: the hero's next turn comes round and is sat out                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `levelUp`      |                                                          | `{ "type": "levelUp" }`: exactly the XP to reach the next level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `loot`         | `amount`: any number, e.g. 3 or -2                       | `{ "type": "loot", "amount": 2 }`: that many random items from the loot pool, into the hero's loot pouch to open; `{ "type": "loot", "items": ["Silver Sword"] }`: that exact prize (any item), into the pouch; `{ "type": "loot", "amount": -2 }`: robbed of that many random items from the pack (never what's worn or in the hidden pocket), and told what was taken |
| `quest`        | `step` (an id from the adventure's quest)                | `{ "type": "quest", "step": "silence-the-bell" }`: completes that step, when it's the one the party is on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Renown is one number per hero, and it can go below 0.

**Movement on the digital board.** `move` pushes the hero now ("Move S 1"): past another hero if one stands there, stopping at the board's edge or an edge that doesn't connect. `freeMovement` widens the hero's **next** move: `extra` squares more ("Free Movement +1"), and/or straight to any free square of the place `orTo` on the tile they're on ("Free Movement or move to any Coin icon"). `moveTo` also lets them go to any square of that place next turn. Plain "Free Movement" needs no effect: it's the normal move. Keep the words in `result` too, for groups playing on the table's board.

New effect types are added in `schema.json`.

## Adding things

- **Location:** add it to the tile's `locations` list with an `id`, `name` and `icon`.
  Icons are [Ionicons](https://icons.expo.fyi/Index) names.
- **Tile:** create `tiles/<id>.json` (the file name must match its `id`) and import it in
  [`src/content/tiles.ts`](../src/content/tiles.ts). The test will remind you if you forget.
- **Action type** (e.g. a future `puzzle`): add its rules to `schema.json`, its type to `src/content/types.ts`,
  its logic to `src/game/actions.ts` and its screen to `src/screens/resolution/`. The tests check that every
  type the schema allows is handled by the app.

## Adventures

Adventure hooks live in [`adventures/`](adventures/), one file each, checked against
[`adventure.schema.json`](adventure.schema.json). Players pick one when starting a New Game (or let fate decide),
and its prologue is read aloud before play.

```json
{
  "$schema": "../adventure.schema.json",
  "id": "the-drowned-bell",
  "status": "draft",
  "party": "group",
  "title": "The Drowned Bell",
  "teaser": "A bell tolls beneath the sea, and the dead are listening.",
  "story": ["Three nights ago…", "{heroes}: you are the only ones foolish enough…"],
  "goal": "Silence the Drowned Bell before the twelfth round ends.",
  "setup": {
    "mode": { "id": "timed", "rounds": 12 },
    "start": { "location": "wilderness.oceans", "note": "Each hero starts on a different space." },
    "inventory": [
      { "type": "gold", "amount": 5 },
      { "type": "card", "name": "Into the Deep" }
    ],
    "firstRound": ["The tide is out: the Oceans can be crossed on foot this round."]
  }
}
```

- `party`: `solo`, `group` or `any`. Solo players only see `solo` and `any` adventures; groups see `group` and `any`.
- `story`: the prologue, one paragraph per entry, shown a paragraph at a time. `{hero}` and `{heroes}` become
  the players' names ("Andrew", "Andrew and Sam", "Andrew, Sam and Riley").
- `goal`: one sentence. Shown at the end of the prologue, from "The Quest" in the menu, and on the Game Over screen.
- `setup` (all optional):
  - `mode`: the suggested mode and round count, pre-filled on the New Game screen. Players can change it.
  - `start`: where every hero's piece starts, as `<tile>.<location>`, with an optional `note`.
  - `inventory`: what each hero starts with, as effects (`gold`, `item`, `card`, `renown`).
  - `firstRound`: special rules for round 1, shown before play and on Home until round 2.
- **Adding one:** create `adventures/<id>.json` (the file name must match its `id`) and list it in
  [`src/content/adventures.ts`](../src/content/adventures.ts). The tests check the schema, that the start location
  exists, that the suggested rounds are allowed, and that it's listed.

## Heroes, items and rules

**Hero classes** live in [`heroes/`](heroes/), one file each, checked against [`hero.schema.json`](hero.schema.json).
Each player picks one when starting a New Game (in a group, the phone is passed around so everyone picks in turn).

```json
{
  "$schema": "../hero.schema.json",
  "id": "warrior",
  "status": "draft",
  "name": "Warrior",
  "description": "Hits things. Asks questions later, if at all.",
  "stats": { "STR": 5, "DEX": 2, "STL": 0, "SUR": 3, "ATK": 5, "DEF": 3 },
  "health": 40,
  "resource": "rage",
  "resourceAmount": 20,
  "renown": 3,
  "abilities": [{ "name": "Hilt Smash" }, { "name": "Brick Wall", "cost": 5, "effect": "..." }],
  "inventory": [
    { "type": "item", "name": "Iron Sword" },
    { "type": "gold", "amount": 3 }
  ]
}
```

- `stats`: how many d6 the hero rolls for each of the six stats. Items can add to them.
- `health`: starting and maximum health. At 0 the hero has fallen (see `rules.json`).
- `resource` / `resourceAmount`: the class's own resource and how much it starts with, which is also
  the most it holds. `resource` effects spend or restore it, never below 0 or above the maximum.
- `renown`: starting renown.
- `abilities`: the class's special abilities, each with a `name` and, once written, a `cost` and an `effect`.
- `inventory`: what the hero starts with, as effects (`gold`, `item`, `card`, `renown`). The adventure's
  starting inventory is added on top.
- **Adding one:** create `heroes/<id>.json` (the file name must match its `id`) and list it in
  [`src/content/heroes.ts`](../src/content/heroes.ts).

**Items** heroes can wear are listed in [`items.json`](items.json) (schema:
[`item.schema.json`](item.schema.json)), e.g. `{ "name": "Silver Sword", "slot": "mainHand", "stats": { "STR": 1 } }`.
The `name` must match the one used in `item` effects and shop items exactly.

- `slot` is where it's worn: `head`, `torso`, `belt`, `pants`, `feet`, `mainHand`, `offHand`,
  `twoHanded` (fills both hands), `necklace` or `ring`. A hero wears **2 necklaces, 10 rings** (one per
  finger) and one of everything else.
- **Only worn items count.** Everything else rides in the pack, which holds `packSize` items (see
  `rules.json`). A new item goes straight on if its place is free, otherwise into the pack.
- Gear can't change while an encounter is being played, so nobody puts on lockpicks just for the lock.
- **Balance:** with ten fingers, rings add up fast. Give most rings and necklaces small, special effects
  rather than raw stats, and make stat rings rare and pricey.
- Items not listed here (or without a `slot`) are just names in the pack.

**Rules** the app shows at the right moment are in [`rules.json`](rules.json) (schema:
[`rules.schema.json`](rules.schema.json)). `death` is shown when a hero's health reaches 0: unless
something saves them, their player pays `goldCost` or loses `renownCost` to be raised with full health, carries on as a class nobody else plays that hasn't fallen this game, or lets their hero rest in peace and leaves the game (their turns are skipped; if every hero rests, the game is over). `packSize` is how
many items a hero can carry besides what they wear.
content/loot.json:
{
  "$schema": "./loot.schema.json",
  "items": [
    { "name": "Iron Sword", "count": 3 },
    { "name": "Lockpicks", "count": 3 },
    { "name": "Health Potion", "count": 3 },
    { "name": "Battered Lute", "count": 3 },
    { "name": "Feathered Hat", "count": 3 },
    { "name": "Silver Sword", "count": 2 },
    { "name": "Onyx Ring", "count": 2 },
    { "name": "Sneaking Boots", "count": 2 },
    { "name": "Spellbook", "count": 2 }
  ],
  "notes": "A starting point (Andrew, 2026-10-23: 'good starting point'): the catalog's everyday items, 3 of the plain ones and 2 of the better ones. The Chest of Fate's rewards are left out. Andrew tunes it."
}
content/rules.json:
{
  "$schema": "./rules.schema.json",
  "status": "draft",
  "packSize": 12,
  "renown": {
    "step": 50,
    "titles": [
